text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach detected on /generate-stream (p99 latency 5.6s over 5m window) — paging @oncall
maya: ack, I'm on it. paging SRE.
raj: looking... can everyone avoid redeploys for now pls
maya: quick metrics: p95=1.2s p99=5.6s, streaming stalls + error rate +3.2%
tess: ML-eng: seeing huge preproc times on tokenizer service. tokenize_ms spiked from ~8 -> 1200ms on many requests
raj: paste sample logs
raj: ```
[2024-05-12T14:02:01Z] req=0xabe tokenizer.tokenize_ms=1123 template_parse_ms=890 json_mode_parse_ms=700 tool_schema_load_ms=150
[2024-05-12T14:02:02Z] req=0xacf tokenizer.tokenize_ms=1189 kv_cache_miss=true
```
maya: that's massive. any recent prompt/template changes?
charlie: infra: no infra deploys. product pushed new prompt templates earlier today with expanded tool schemas
lena: product: rolled out nested JSON tool-schemas for customers A,B this morning — intended to support richer tool calls
tess: JSON-mode parsing + eager tool schema load is blowing up preproc CPU and stalls streaming flushes
raj: short-term mitigations proposed:
  1) route streaming to fallback model-compact for pages >=256 tokens
  2) disable JSON-mode prompt parsing globally on hosted until we patch
  3) enable prefix caching for recent prompts to reduce tokenize path
maya: can someone flip the JSON-mode flag for hosted? i can coordinate customer comms
charlie: i can flip infra feature flag. command:
charlie: ```
curl -X POST "https://config.internal/api/flags/set" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"flag":"prompt_json_mode","value":false}'
```
raj: will that require a rollout or pod restarts?
charlie: instant flag, but preproc reads flag on startup — will restart preproc pods to pick it up
charlie: executing flag change now
charlie: :white_check_mark: flag `prompt_json_mode` set to false for hosted cluster
incident-bot: [INFO] flag change applied, affected hosts: preproc-*/v2
deploy-bot: restarting preproc pods to pick up flag
deploy-bot: ```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/preproc -n inference
```
maya: heads-up: disabling JSON-mode changes behavior for customers using structured parsing — we should send notice
lena: agreed. initiating customer notify for A,B
customer-notify-bot: queued notification to customers: A,B — template: "We detected latency issues and temporarily disabled structured JSON parsing to mitigate impact. We'll restore when fixes are in place."
raj: monitoring: p99 dropped from 5.6s -> 1.8s within 2m of the flag change
maya: p95 back to ~0.9s; p99 trending down to 1.6s — streaming error rate normalizing :thumbsup:
tess: ML will prepare a fix: optimized JSON parser + lazy tool-schema load; ETA ~4h for a canary build
raj: followups we need:
  - SRE-4321: add defensive limits on tool_schema size + fail-fast for gigantic templates
  - Telemetry: emit tokenize_ms per template id so we can alert earlier
  - Prefill prefix cache for top-100 templates (backfill job)
  - Product: consider rolling back today's template expansion for worst-offenders
maya: i'm handing off oncall to charlie for overnight monitoring. summary to include root cause + mitigations + customer impact
charlie: taking oncall. summary: 
  - root cause: expensive JSON-mode prompt templates + large tool schema loads increased tokenizer/preproc CPU and tail latency
  - mitigations applied: disabled JSON-mode, restarted preproc, routed heavy streams to fallback model, enabled prefix cache
  - customer impact: degraded streaming for customers A,B for ~15m; notifications sent
charlie: contact points: raj (SRE), tess (ML), lena (product)
maya: thanks. if p99 creeps back up @maya please wake me (page)
raj: opened incident ticket SRE-4321 (investigate telemetry + limits)
tess: creating ML ticket ML-987 (optimize-json-parser + lazy-tool-load)
maya: i'll write the incident report later and attach logs/graphs. closing the page after handoff. :lock_with_ink_pen:
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] SLO back within target, closing page
